item.title: McDonald’s once sold beloved cookies featuring forgotten characters from the chain's past
item.description: McDonald's discontinued McDonaldland Cookies featured Grimace and Ronald McDonald faces with a subtle lemon flavor that fans still crave decades later.
item.content:encoded:
Introduced in 1974, McDonaldland Cookies became a regular addition to McDonald’s Happy Meals when they debuted nationwide in 1979, but the beloved menu item was discontinued in the early 2000s, to the disappointment of many fans.

The small, crunchy, cookies were baked for McDonald’s by Keebler, had a subtle lemon flavor and featured the faces of beloved McDonald’s characters like Grimace, Ronald McDonald, Birdie, and Hamburglar.

Customers described them as a cross between shortbread and animal crackers, and McDonaldland Cookies came in either a little plastic bag or a brightly colored cardboard box that also showed the faces of McDonald’s characters.

The fast food chain altered its Happy Meals to include healthier items such as apple slices in the early 2000s.

MCDONALD'S REVIVES DECADES-OLD FAVORITE FOR AMERICA 250 AFTER YEARS OF CUSTOMER REQUESTS

Between 2003 and 2004, McDonaldland Cookies were discontinued at all U.S. locations.

Chocolate chip cookies, however, remained on the menu.

McDonald’s has been serving some variation of chocolate chip cookies since the early 1970s, with today's chewy, soft-baked version introduced in 2012.

MCDONALD'S BRINGS BACK POPULAR ITEM FOR SHORT TIME AS ONE STATE GETS A TREAT

Although McDonaldland Cookies are no longer available in the United States, select McDonald’s locations in Australia still offer them, and certain New Zealand restaurants serve the treat under the name "McHappy Cookies."

Fans have also shared on Reddit that a cookie with a flavor and texture similar to the original McDonaldland cookies is available at Aldi supermarkets.

AMERICA'S FAVORITE FAST-FOOD CHAIN NAMED: MCDONALD'S WINS HEARTS BUT NOT BEST BURGER, SURVEY SAYS

One Reddit user commented: "I am eating the Benton's animal crackers from Aldi right now and they taste exactly like the McDonaldland cookies."

McDonaldland Cookies might be gone in the U.S., but the characters have not been totally forgotten.

The viral Grimace Shake, a purple-hued milkshake with a vanilla soft serve base and mixed berry flavoring, came out in 2023 as a limited-time treat to celebrate the beloved character’s birthday.

Beginning in 2022, McDonald's sporadically released various limited-edition Adult Happy Meals, allowing grownups to enjoy the nostalgia of Happy Meals — which, depending on their age, might have included McDonaldland Cookies.

Fox News Digital reached out to McDonald's for comment.

item.title: Keenan Allen faces NFL suspension after blood alcohol level nearly triple the legal limit: report
item.description: Keenan Allen's blood alcohol level was nearly triple the legal limit, which should trigger the NFL's substance abuse policy and potential suspension.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL could be dishing out a suspension to Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen after he was charged this week with two misdemeanors stemming from his arrest on charges of drunk driving before the start of the season.

Allen is facing preliminary charges of operating a motor vehicle while intoxicated (OVWI) as well as OVWI endangering a person, which are both misdemeanors in Indiana.

However, Allen had a blood alcohol level of .224 when he was arrested, which is almost triple the legal limit of .08, per Yahoo Sports. The high BAC is a higher Class A misdemeanor in Indiana.

Allen’s arrest violates the NFL’s substance-abuse policy, and a minimum three-game suspension follows the violation per the league’s Collective Bargaining Agreement. If the player is more intoxicated, a longer suspension could be in play.

It was reported the NFL would be waiting on Allen’s legal proceedings before issuing a suspension.

With an attorney conference expected on Oct. 26, Allen’s suspension could be coming mid-season for Indianapolis.

As a result, Allen is available to play for the Colts in their Week 2 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs on "Sunday Night Football."

The 34-year-old receiver also played last week, hauling in six of Daniel Jones’ passes for 32 yards in the 41-23 loss to the Baltimore Ravens.

Allen is in his 14th NFL season, his first with the Colts after signing a one-year deal with the team this off-season. His stardom came with the Los Angeles Chargers, whom he spent 12 seasons with, including a reunion this past year.

Allen caught 81 passes in his Chargers return last season for 77 yards and four touchdowns. The year prior, Allen was away from the West Coast for the first time, playing with the Chicago Bears during the 2024 campaign.

item.title: Massage clients report bizarre flu-like reaction after popular spa treatment
item.description: Massage flu symptoms like soreness, fatigue and headaches are real, but experts debunk the popular claim that massages release toxins from the body.
item.content:encoded:
A popular wellness treatment is allegedly leaving some people with unexpected symptoms, including aches, fatigue and headaches.

Social media users have described feeling under the weather after getting a massage, with some saying they feel as though they are coming down with an illness.

The reaction is sometimes referred to online as "massage flu," though health experts say it is not an actual medical diagnosis.

DO RED LIGHT THERAPY AND COLD PLUNGES REALLY WORK? A DOCTOR REVEALS THE TRUTH

"This phenomenon is something I have definitely heard of and had patients tell me," W. Zach Smith, a Seattle-based physical therapist and co-founder of HIDEF Physical Therapy, told Fox News Digital.

"The idea of this has been around a long time but usually described as fatigue and soreness," Smith said. "The flu part of the name I have heard more recently."

Soreness can happen when a lot of pressure is applied to the muscles for a long period of time, especially if someone is not used to getting massages, Smith added.

"Any time you go in and apply a lot of pressure to a muscle for a long period of time, it can essentially bruise the tissue," he said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

The body may also have a mild inflammatory response after a massage, which can contribute to soreness, Smith said.

Drew Voelsch, a chiropractor at Forza Chiropractic in Illinois, said he has also heard patients refer to the reaction as "massage flu" or an "adjustment hangover."

"The symptoms are real," Voelsch told Fox News Digital, pointing to soreness, fatigue and mild headaches that may last 24 to 48 hours. "The label is social media."

A massage around the neck, scalp or jaw can also trigger headaches because those areas can be involved in tension headaches, according to Smith.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Both experts pushed back on the idea that these symptoms are caused by a massage "releasing toxins" from the body, a claim that has circulated in social media comments.

"This is a myth," Smith said. "There is no basis or science behind this."

Voelsch agreed, noting that the liver and kidneys handle the body's waste-removal processes.

To help reduce discomfort, Smith recommended asking for less pressure or a shorter massage and gradually working up to deeper or longer sessions.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Voelsch also suggested drinking water, eating something light beforehand and moving gently afterward.

Mild soreness is typically not a cause for concern, but Smith said new or persistent pain may be a reason to contact a doctor.

"If you are having a new, unexplained pain that is persistent, that would be a good time to call your doctor," he said.

Voelsch recommended seeking medical advice if symptoms last longer than about 72 hours or include fever, sharp or radiating pain, numbness or tingling, spreading swelling or bruising, or faintness.

item.title: ICE shooting rocks Austin as Democrat demands bodycam video, independent probe
item.description: Rep. Greg Casar claims ICE shot a person in Austin, Texas, and demands body camera footage and a full independent investigation into Sunday's operation.
item.content:encoded:
A Democratic congressman is demanding answers after claiming an ICE officer shot someone during a Sunday morning operation in Austin, Texas.

Austin city leaders will address what the city described as an "Immigration and Customs Enforcement shooting" during a 4 p.m. news conference Sunday at Austin City Hall. Mayor Kirk Watson, Austin Police Chief Lisa Davis and Austin-Travis County EMS Chief Robert Luckritz are scheduled to speak about the incident.

The Texas Department of Public Safety confirmed to FOX 7 Austin that U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement was handling an investigation in the 7000 block of West Anderson Lane but did not say whether anyone was shot or injured.

"ICE investigation confirmed in the 7000 block of West Anderson, ICE is handling investigation," a DPS public information officer told the outlet.

'SQUAD' MEMBER CALLS DHS 'GREATEST THREAT TO OUR SAFETY' AFTER ICE-INVOLVED SHOOTING

Rep. Greg Casar, D-Texas, claimed in a post on X that "ICE has shot a person in Austin this morning" and called for a full, independent investigation and the immediate release of body-camera footage.

"Over and over, ICE has shot people and then lied about what happened," Casar wrote. "We will demand truth, transparency and accountability."

ICE AGENTS IN FATAL HOUSTON SHOOTING WERE NOT WEARING BODY CAMERAS, SOURCES SAY

Authorities have not released details of the shooting.

The Austin investigation comes amid heightened tensions over federal immigration enforcement operations across the country.

ANTI-ICE PROTESTERS CLASH WITH AGENTS OUTSIDE NEW JERSEY DETENTION CENTER AS GOV SHERRILL DENIED ENTRY

Clashes erupted outside New Jersey's Delaney Hall immigration detention center in May after protesters defied a state police order to move to a designated demonstration area. Newark Mayor Ras Baraka later criticized the tactics used by state troopers sent to secure the facility, which had become the focus of frequent demonstrations.

Federal immigration operations also drew national scrutiny in Minnesota following the fatal shootings of Renee Good and Alex Pretti in Minneapolis. Good was killed by an ICE agent in early January after authorities said she tried to use her vehicle to run over federal officers, while Pretti was fatally shot by agents on Jan. 24 as he recorded federal officers.

The Austin Police Department referred Fox News Digital to ICE for further information.

Fox News Digital reached out to ICE and the Texas Department of Public Safety for additional information and comment.

item.title: Trump, Iranian president converge on NYC for ‘dramatic’ UN showdown as Tehran faces tight restrictions
item.description: President Donald Trump and Masoud Pezeshkian converge on New York City for the U.N. General Assembly amid strict U.S. restrictions on Iran's delegation movements.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian are set to converge on New York City for the U.N. General Assembly (UNGA) this week, setting up what former White House officials describe as a "dramatic" diplomatic moment, with Tehran’s delegation effectively "captive" under U.S. restrictions amid heightened Middle East tensions.

Pezeshkian, for one, is scheduled to address the assembly on Wednesday, Reuters and Iran's semi-official news agency, Mehr, reported Sunday, with Trump at the rostrum on Tuesday.

"The choreography here is going to make for a fairly dramatic moment," Theo Wold, former acting assistant attorney general and White House domestic policy advisor, told Fox News Digital.

PUTIN, XI AND IRAN'S PEZESHKIAN DESCEND ON INDIA FOR HIGH-STAKES BRICS SUMMIT AMID ESCALATING GLOBAL TENSIONS

"For the Iranians, the limitation is going to be that there's going to be less access to the international press and less ability for them to essentially poke the Trump administration in the eye," Wold added before noting that it is "pretty sensible to allow them to participate in the international forum and to discuss whatever issues they think are pertinent to their regime and then tell them to go home."

The high-profile gathering also comes as Trump weighs renewed strikes on Iran amid the almost seven-month war. Tehran, meanwhile, has set seven conditions for talks with Washington, according to Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei.

Iran also warned on Sunday against any big new attack by the United States and its allies, saying it had information such a move was being prepared, Reuters reported.

While the U.S. approved visas for Iran’s delegation earlier this week, including Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, the State Department has placed strict limits on Iranian movements while in Manhattan.

As the host country under a 1947 U.N. agreement, the United States generally must facilitate the entry and transit of foreign representatives traveling to U.N. headquarters, including officials from adversarial nations.

"While ordinary Iranians endure brutal repression, water and electricity shortages, and soaring inflation, the regime's officials want to go on shopping sprees in New York. Not on our watch," U.S. State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said on X.

UN WATCHDOG SLAMS POTENTIAL ELECTION OF IRAN TO PANEL WITH HUMAN RIGHTS SWAY: 'LUNATICS RUNNING THE ASYLUM'

For Washington, Wold said the U.S. is not obligated to give them unrestricted access beyond diplomatic responsibilities.

"Here, the delegation will be restricted to their accommodation in New York City and the U.N. headquarters there in Manhattan," Wold clarified.

He characterized the move by Washington as a way of telling the delegation it could participate in official discussions but not "go and buy a bunch of microwaves or a small car at Costco or a dealership in the greater New York area."

"Some of the restrictions fully recognize that when Iran comes to New York for UNGA, really it's about them lining their pockets and going on shopping sprees to get household appliances and Rolex watches," Wold said. "They're not going to be going on shopping sprees. They're certainly not going to be hitting up Michelin-starred restaurants in greater Manhattan.

"They also go to Sam’s Club and Walmart and Costco. And that was one of the specific prohibitions issued by the State Department this week: to contact those big-box retailers that require a basic membership and say, ‘You’re not to transact or do any business with Iranians when they arrive, and you’re to notify us when they do.’"

KUSHNER TOUTS UNPRECEDENTED IRAN CONTACTS AS TEHRAN DENIES TRUMP BACKCHANNEL

Despite the restrictions, Wold said UNGA gives Washington the opportunity it has "wanted for quite some time to have a large enough audience, and a sort of captive Iranian delegation" to make some of the essential points for why the administration pursued the actions it did against the Iranian regime.

Iranian state media also reported Sept. 19 that Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said New York held "absolutely no charm" for the Iranian delegation.

Baghaei, Mehr News Agency reported, went on to accuse the U.S. of using every tool to block the delegation’s participation, asserting that Iran’s attendance is a legal right rather than a favor.

Wold went on to criticize the U.N. for hosting state representatives hostile to American interests while raising security concerns.

"It's going to be one of those things that's fairly perplexing to most Americans," Wold said. "How is it that the representatives of what we have long identified as a hostile regime, but now one that we're actually engaged in combat operations against, one that has killed American service members, why is it that their diplomats get to come to the United Nations and exchange niceties with other kleptocrats or some of their other allies on the international scene?"

TWO US SERVICE MEMBERS KILLED IN IRANIAN STRIKES ON JORDAN, CENTCOM SAYS

Wold also added that the United Nations wants to "lecture us about international climate change or the need to trans children, but the other is happy to sort of serve as a forum for obvious violators of human rights and obvious regimes that are contrary to any number of internationally agreed-upon protocols."

Amid the hostility between Washington and Tehran, Wold said the gathering could also provide an opening for diplomacy. Trump is also slated to hold bilateral and sideline meetings with leaders from the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) to discuss regional security and the Strait of Hormuz.

"There's the hope that there'll be an opportunity for real discussion," Wold said of UNGA. "Everyone's hope, especially from State Department leadership, is that there'll be an opportunity to have a fulsome, sort of meaningful discussion with the Iranians, freed from some of the theatrics the Iranians have engaged in.

"There's a hope that there'll be an opportunity for closed-door private discussions between the United States and Iranians and really try to hammer out some kind of agreement about what a cessation of hostilities will look like."

Wold expressed confidence in Washington’s posture heading into the summit.

"The president is best equipped for these moments. This is really where he sort of shines as a natural leader," he said. "He's not one to bend or to break. It's a precarious time for President Trump, but I have no doubt at all that he'll rise to the moment."

item.title: Massachusetts' plan to offer postpartum screening home visits sparks online debate
item.description: Massachusetts Gov. Maura Healey is investing $2.25 million to send nurses into homes of new parents, sparking a heated government overreach debate.
item.content:encoded:
Massachusetts is expanding a taxpayer-funded program that sends nurses into the homes of new parents after childbirth, fueling debate over the government's role in family health care.

Gov. Maura Healey recently announced plans to invest $2 million to expand the state's Welcome Family program, which offers voluntary home visits from registered nurses after the birth of a child. Healey also proposed an additional $250,000 to strengthen the Massachusetts Child Psychiatry Access Program for Moms, which provides mental health support to providers caring for pregnant and postpartum patients.

"Everybody in the state, when you have a baby, you're going to have a home visit within days, weeks and that will be an opportunity for a healthcare provider to make an assessment to see if you need some additional support and resources," Healey said during an interview last week on Boston Public Radio.

CLANCY HOLDOUT JUROR TAPS FORMER TRUMP LAWYER TO FIGHT BACK AS HE'S 'DRAGGED THROUGH THE MUD': ATTORNEY

Healey also said the state is investing in training healthcare providers to better identify the signs of postpartum mental health conditions.

The announcement comes amid heightened public attention to postpartum mental health in Massachusetts during the high-profile trial of Lindsay Clancy, the former labor and delivery nurse accused of killing her three young children in January 2023. In a case ultimately declared a mistrial because of a deadlocked jury, Clancy's defense argued she was suffering from severe postpartum mental illness. The case has reignited debate over how postpartum mental health conditions are identified and treated.

LINDSAY CLANCY'S FAMILY WAS 'VERY CONCERNED' ABOUT HER MENTAL HEALTH IN THE MONTHS BEFORE SHE KILLED HER KIDS

State officials say the program is intended to improve maternal health outcomes by connecting families with additional support.

The announcement also sparked debate on social media, where some users questioned whether the program represented an appropriate role for government. "Doctors and pediatricians are more than capable to conduct appropriate screenings for their patients. Say no to home visits," one user wrote on X, while another called the program "creepy" and "massive government overreach."

Not everyone opposed the proposal outright. "More overreach. However, if it's an offer, and not a mandate, it could be a good thing for some young families and single moms," comedian Bob Phillips wrote on X.

The reaction reflects a broader national debate over how states should balance maternal mental health, taxpayer costs, individual privacy and the role government should play in supporting new families.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Massachusetts Department of Public Health and Healey's office for additional comment.

item.title: Dakota Johnson hopes to start a family after career kept her 'gone for 20 years'
item.description: Dakota Johnson reveals she feels "a soul that wants to come through" as she opens up about hoping for motherhood before her "Verity" premiere.
item.content:encoded:
Dakota Johnson thought her life would look a lot different than it does now.

During a recent interview with Vogue, the 36-year-old actress spoke about her career and whether she sees herself starting a family, telling the outlet it's something she really wants for herself.

"I really do. I do, but for whatever reason, that’s the plan of the universe," she said. "So I would love that. I hope that that happens for me. I’ve always felt, especially the last few years, that there is a soul that wants to come through. And I hope that I’m lucky enough to be able to do that."

She went on to say that it can sometimes be hard to be around her friends and co-stars who have children or are starting their families when "things turned out differently than I thought," but says she is still "hopeful for that."

LADY GAGA AND FIANCÉ MICHAEL POLANSKY WELCOME THEIR FIRST CHILD TOGETHER: REPORT

Johnson made a name for herself throughout the 2010s, starring in films such as "The Social Network" and "21 Jump Street," before landing the role of Anastasia Steele in "Fifty Shades of Grey," which became her breakout role.

She continued building her resume, starring in films such as "Peanut Butter Falcon," "Madame Web" and "The Materialists," but it looks like she plans on slowing down soon.

"I’ve worked back-to-back for so long that now I have this deep calling to shift my perspective a bit and maybe have a bit more of a real life," she said. "I’ve been gone for, like, 20 years. The people in my life are so used to me leaving for months at a time."

Her main goal is to live her life authentically, noting, "I want to unfold and unfold and really lovingly embrace this life."

Johnson is gearing up for the premiere of her latest movie, "Verity," a psychological thriller based on the novel by Colleen Hoover, which also stars Josh Hartnett and Anne Hathaway.

The "Splitsville" actress plays Lowen Ashleigh in the film, a ghostwriter who is hired to finish writing a book series written by Verity Crawford after she suffers an injury, but soon finds things aren't exactly as they seem.

"Michael Showalter, the director, would give me direction that was so extremely camp, and that’s not really me as an artist," Johnson said about the role. "But it was so fun, and our references and guidelines were all these erotic thrillers that people are like, Okay, this is ridiculous, but I’m enjoying myself."

Johnson is no stranger to the demands of Hollywood, as she comes from a family of acting royalty. Her mother is Academy Award-nominated actress Melanie Griffith, and her father is "Miami Vice" star Don Johnson. Her maternal grandmother is actress Tippi Hedren.

item.title: Mom gives birth in KFC parking lot and gives newborn fitting fast-food nickname
item.description: Katie Murphy delivered baby Cody in a Kentucky Fried Chicken parking lot in Bromsgrove, Worcestershire, England, earning him the name Colonel Cody.
item.content:encoded:
A mother had a unique labor and delivery experience on Aug. 29, giving birth to her baby boy in the parking lot of a KFC restaurant in Bromsgrove, a town in Worcestershire, England.

Katie Murphy, 33, and her partner Stephen Kirby, 32, welcomed their son Cody into the world under untraditional circumstances, prompting them to give him a nickname inspired by KFC's famous founder, Colonel Harland Sanders, news agency SWNS reported.

THE KFC MENU ITEM COLONEL SANDERS HATED BECAME ONE OF THE CHAIN'S BIGGEST STAPLES

The couple, who also have a 4-year-old daughter, had gone to the hospital that morning thinking Katie was going into labor, but they went home around 4 p.m. after being told it was still too early to deliver the baby.

However, Katie's contractions persisted for hours, and at about 9 p.m., the couple decided to return to the hospital.

About halfway through the roughly 30-minute drive, "Katie said she could feel something and knew the baby was coming," Stephen recalled.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

While on the phone with emergency services, Stephen spotted a KFC restaurant that he and Katie frequented, and he pulled into the parking lot.

Before the ambulance arrived, baby Cody made his entrance into the world. Stephen ran around to the front seat where Katie was sitting and opened the door just in time to catch the couple's newborn son, who emerged at 9:35 p.m., SWNS reported.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"It all happened so fast. Thankfully, the ambulance was with us about five minutes later and took us to hospital," Katie said. She also noted that Cody is perfectly healthy and happy, "despite his abrupt entrance into the world in his dad's car."

Cody's memorable arrival earned him a KFC-inspired nickname: Colonel Cody.

"It was decided that we have to take him to KFC for his first birthday and get him his first weekend job there," Katie said.

A KFC spokesperson commented: "We're honored to have been the place of Cody's birth and are sending bucket loads of love to the whole family, along with some KFC merch and vouchers to help them celebrate."

"We can't wait to welcome them back for a meal to mark the occasion," the spokesperson added.

item.title: Bears quarterback Caleb Williams carted off at Soldier Field with apparent hamstring injury
item.description: Caleb Williams grabbed his hamstring while escaping a tackle from Andrew Van Ginkel and was carted to the locker room during the Bears-Vikings game.
item.content:encoded:
The Chicago Bears are holding their breath because Caleb Williams is injured and had to be helped off the field by two trainers who held him up as he limped.

After he reached the sideline, Williams was taken to the team's medical tent and then was carted to the Bears' locker room for further medical assistance.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Williams grabbed at his right hamstring as he was trying to escape a tackle from Vikings linebacker Andrew Van Ginkel. He writhed in pain on the field until help arrived.

The Bears announced Williams suffered a hamstring injury. He did not return to the game against the Vikings.

When he left the field, Williams implored the home crowd at Soldier Field and gave them a thumbs up.

It is unclear how this injury will impact that team's season until an MRI can determine the injury's severity.

"We'll know tomorrow," Bears coach Ben Johnson said.

The concern, even if a hamstring injury sounds mundane, is whether it is merely strained or torn.

If it is torn, the injury could take between 3–6 months to recover, depending on the severity of the tear. A less severe hamstring injury could be a 1–3 week recovery time.

Backup, Tyson Bagent, took over at quarterback for the Bears after Williams departed.

The Bears lost this game against the Vikings and a season that began with high hopes is in limbo for the moment.

Williams, in his third NFL season after making significant progress in 2025 under first-year head coach Ben Johnson, led the Bears to an 11–6 record, the NFC North title and their first playoff appearance since 2020 while setting a franchise record with 3,942 passing yards and producing 31 total touchdowns. 

Williams carried that momentum into the 2026 opener, completing 21 of 29 passes for 269 yards and two touchdowns while rushing for 65 yards and two more scores in Chicago’s 59-37 victory over Carolina.

"I'm actually happy it's nothing with the knee," Johnson said. "That was my first inclination. But, yeah, a hamstring could be pretty damaging as well.

"We'll see how bad it is tomorrow."

item.title: Xi prepares China ‘for battle’ as expert warns of grave danger facing US ahead of DC summit
item.description: China expert Gordon Chang claims Xi Jinping is preparing China for war against the U.S. as President Donald Trump hosts a high-stakes summit Thursday.
item.content:encoded:
As President Donald Trump touts a productive relationship with China ahead of his summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping, an expert is warning that the U.S. is in a "very dangerous period" in its relations with the communist nation, claiming that Xi is preparing for war.

Trump and Xi are set to meet on Thursday in Washington, D.C., just four months after the leader’s last meeting in May, with artificial intelligence and trade expected to be at the forefront of the conversation.

Gatestone Institute senior fellow Gordon Chang claimed that, despite the leaders trumpeting a positive relationship, Xi is mulling a war against the United States and organizing troops "for battle."

TRUMP SAYS CHINESE PRESIDENT XI JINPING WILL VISIT US ON SEPT 24

"Xi Jinping keeps on talking about going to war against us… and also he's preparing China's society, civilian and military, for battle. And we think we're at peace," Chang said Sunday on "Fox News Live." "So, this is a very dangerous period for us."

Chang’s remarks come amid reports that China aided Iran in attacks that killed three U.S. troops in Jordan earlier this summer.

TRUMP SAYS CHINA 'SPIES' ON US AFTER REPORT TIES CHINESE IMAGERY TO IRAN STRIKE

Iran reportedly received satellite images of an airbase in Jordan from Chinese entities before carrying out the attack, according to the Wall Street Journal.

Chang decried China for providing "targeting data" to Iran that resulted in the deaths of U.S. service members, saying Trump must "absolutely" get tougher on China and arguing that decades of open dialogue with the Chinese have only made things worse for the United States.

EXPERT WARNS CHINA ALREADY WAGING ‘UNRESTRICTED WARFARE’ AGAINST US THROUGH FENTANYL, ESPIONAGE AND SABOTAGE

"Whatever one thinks of the strategic discussions the United States has with China, there's this moral dimension that China is deliberately killing Americans," he said.

Experts expect this week’s summit with Trump and Xi to be vastly different from their May meeting, as since then, conflict in the Middle East has escalated and the AI race has intensified.

CHINA EXPERT WARNS BEIJING WANTS AMERICANS – NOT THE CCP – TO SPREAD ITS MESSAGE

Chang believes Trump will not get any better of a reception about AI than former President Joe Biden did during his meeting with Xi in 2023, adding that the Chinese leader is not positioned to compromise.

"Xi Jinping is facing a turbulent Communist Party at home, which means that he can't compromise. Also, he's arrogant. He incorrectly believes that China's on the way up and the United States is on the way down and we're in terminal decline," Chang explained.

"He's not very much inclined in any event to compromise with the United States," he added.

item.title: Cops flush homecoming prank plans after seizing 650 toilet paper rolls in ‘Operation Clean Sweep’
item.description: Plainfield police seized 650 rolls of toilet paper in "Operation Clean Sweep" after masked groups targeted homes near Plainfield North High School.
item.content:encoded:
After warning students not to let homecoming pranks cross the line, an Illinois police department found itself staring down one very unusual haul.

Plainfield police intercepted a massive toilet paper stash allegedly headed for neighborhood homes after reports of masked groups targeting the area near Plainfield North High School.

"And yes… 650 rolls. We counted," police said.

Police displayed the haul under an "Operation Clean Sweep" banner and jokingly gave it an estimated "street value" of $1,708.66 after two nights of escalating complaints from the surrounding community.

TRENDING 'SENIOR ASSASSIN' GAME DRAWS STARK WARNINGS FROM POLICE NATIONWIDE: 'DANGEROUS MISUNDERSTANDINGS'

"Homecoming is not a free pass to damage someone else's property or disrupt their quality of life," the department wrote on Facebook.

FLORIDA POLICE DEPARTMENT GOES VIRAL WITH GENIUS STRATEGY TO CONNECT WITH COMMUNITY

Officers received double-digit calls for service involving teens on both Monday and Tuesday during a two-hour period beginning shortly after 7 p.m. in the area surrounding the high school, according to police.

Residents reported that homes and vehicles had been targeted with toilet paper, eggs, ketchup, detergent pods and other items. Police said groups of 20 to 25 people wearing hoodies and ski masks would "pull up" in several vehicles at the same time and "cause chaos."

STUDENT CHARGED, WEAPON RECOVERED AFTER 3 TEENS TARGETED IN INCIDENT LINKED TO HIGH SCHOOL TRADITION: POLICE

The targets were not limited to friends or classmates. Some of the homes belonged to families with small children or residents with no children at all, police said.

"At this point, we are seeing property damage and significant cleanup, and residents are understandably frustrated," the department wrote.

COPS HALT PLANNED 'TEEN TAKEOVER' AS OFFICIALS BRACE FOR A SUMMER SURGE IN CHAOS AND ARRESTS: POLICE CHIEF

The department also made clear that the homecoming calls were pulling police attention from more serious incidents.

Officers assisted firefighters at a structure fire, helped Illinois State Police, made a DUI arrest and responded to crashes, intoxicated people, violations of protection orders and a family experiencing a mental health crisis, according to the post.

"In short, we DO have better things to do," police wrote. "So PLEASE, be respectful of your community and let us!"

Police had laid out a "zero-tolerance approach" ahead of homecoming week, warning that pranks involving trespassing, property damage or dangerous behavior could bring criminal charges.

item.title: Bengals' Ja'Marr Chase scores jaw-dropping first touchdown of the season after lackluster Week 1 start
item.description: Cincinnati Bengals star Chase contorted his body along the sideline to snag a jaw-dropping touchdown catch against the Houston Texans defense.
item.content:encoded:
It was a quiet week for Cincinnati Bengals star receiver Ja’Marr Chase in the team’s home opener against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

But Chase never stays quiet for long in the NFL, and he proved it with his first touchdown grab of the season against the Houston Texans, that you must see to believe.

In classic Chase fashion, it was jaw-dropping.

Both defenses started this game at NRG Stadium with stellar play. In turn, neither team found their way onto the scoreboard in the first quarter.

However, the Bengals’ defense came through with a big shift of momentum, as Dexter Lawrence burst through the offensive line and tackled Texans running back David Montgomery to turn the ball over on downs as Houston couldn’t find the line to gain.

item.title: Ms Rachel calls Gaza journalist ‘friend’ in resurfaced clip after he admits hiding Oct 7 hostage footage
item.description: Children's YouTube star Ms. Rachel faces scrutiny after a resurfaced video shows her calling Motaz Azaiza her "friend" amid his Oct. 7 revelations.
item.content:encoded:
Children's YouTube star Ms. Rachel faced renewed scrutiny on Sunday after a 2025 video of her calling Palestinian photojournalist Motaz Azaiza her "friend," resurfaced, days after Azaiza admitted he deliberately withheld footage of Israeli hostages being beaten by a crowd in Gaza on Oct. 7, 2023.

The short video appears to show Ms. Rachel, whose real name is Rachel Griffin Accurso, introducing Azaiza to her young audience while teaching the letter "M."

"Hi, yes, it’s M, for my friend, Motaz. Yay! Bye!" Accurso said.

MS RACHEL CONFRONTED ON ACCUSING ISRAEL OF 'GENOCIDE' IN PARK INTERACTION WITH PODCASTER

The video was originally shared on Instagram and later removed, according to reporting from July 2025.

Azaiza, who amassed millions of social media followers documenting the war in Gaza, appeared briefly in the clip and greeted Ms. Rachel.

The video also took on new significance after Azaiza described earlier this month what he witnessed during the Hamas-led Oct. 7, 2023, terrorist attack in an extensive interview with journalist Ahmed al-Biqawi on the Arabic-language "Taqarrab" podcast. Azaiza said he followed a vehicle carrying Israeli captives and filmed as members of a crowd assaulted them.

Azaiza said he didn't publish the video, however, as he feared it could put the Palestinians involved at risk.

"I saw the vehicle of the Al-Qassam Brigades, and there were Israeli captives there," Azaiza said. "People got out, watched, beat them, hit them, and I followed them and filmed. But I did not publish those videos. Why? Because I did not want to ruin the lives of the people who were filmed."

MS RACHEL POSTS SUPPORT FOR HIJAB-WEARING KINDERGARTNERS AFTER TRUMP POST

Azaiza said he withheld the footage because he believed Israeli authorities could use it to identify the Palestinians appearing in the videos.

"I understood that Israel would use those videos to identify every person who was there and eliminate them," Azaiza said. "I did not want to be responsible, even indirectly, for the deaths of those people in exchange for a few likes and views online."

NEW YORK TIMES ISSUES CORRECTION, DELETES LINE QUESTIONING IF ISRAELIS WERE VICTIMS OF OCT 7 TERROR ATTACK

Azaiza also criticized Hamas and described the restrictions faced by journalists working inside Gaza. He said photographers learned to lower their cameras when Palestinians criticized Hamas because showing such dissent could lead to retaliation.

Despite describing himself as a supporter of armed Palestinian resistance, Azaiza said Hamas' actions had failed to protect Palestinians living in Gaza.

"I support armed resistance, but one that brings results, or at least gives me the feeling that my life is valuable in the eyes of the resistance," Azaiza said. "Why should a Palestinian be cheap in the eyes of Palestinians themselves? You are making people hate the resistance with your own hands."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE
 

Azaiza's profile rose dramatically after the war began. Time named him to its 2024 list of the world's 100 most influential people for his photographs documenting Gaza.

Rabbi Yaakov Menken, executive vice president of the Coalition for Jewish Values, told Fox News Digital that Azaiza’s disclosure raised questions about his journalistic judgment and his decision to withhold the footage.

"After years spent claiming to share what was happening in Gaza ‘unfiltered,’ Azaiza revealed that he hid footage — not, per journalistic norms, to protect victims from further harm, but because he didn't want Israel to arrest the perpetrators. Innocent civilians had been kidnapped, already sexually abused, and his concern was with the people that beat them and rejoiced at Hamas' crimes. That speaks volumes about his journalism and his moral character," Menken said.

Accurso, meanwhile, has become increasingly outspoken about Gaza.

Last week, she accused celebrities and other public figures who had remained silent about Palestinian children of applying a racial double standard.

"They probably would say something if these kids were White and from a different place," Accurso said. "Please stop being racist and risk something."

Elizabeth Barcohana, the California Republican Party’s Jewish engagement chair, told Fox News Digital that she believed Accurso’s Gaza advocacy was spreading misleading information to her large audience.

"Ms. Rachel is essentially sanitizing terrorism with false and misleading information to emotionally manipulate her very impressionable following and those around her in her industry," Barcohana said.

Fox News Digital reached out to Ms. Rachel for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: Fat Bear Week bracket is set: meet the heavyweights, underdogs and defending champ in this year's tournament
item.description: Forget March Madness. Fat Bear Week returns to Katmai National Park with 16 brown bears as defending champ Chunk faces rising star Bucky on Wednesday.
item.content:encoded:
Forget March Madness. The most important bracket of the year has arrived.

Fat Bear Week is back, baby!

The annual competition at Alaska's Katmai National Park and Preserve kicks off Tuesday with 16 brown bears vying for the title of chonkiest champ. This year's bracket features a defending champion, a few rising stars and some heavyweight opening-round matchups.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

Here's how it works: Two bears face off in a single-elimination tournament, and fans vote for the one they believe has done the best job packing on the pounds ahead of winter hibernation.

More than 1.7 million votes were cast during last year's competition, which saw Bear 32 — better known as "Chunk" — claim the title.

Now, the reigning champ is back for another shot at glory. But he's got some serious competition.

Chunk won last year's competition despite suffering a broken jaw in June 2025, likely during a fight with another bear. The injury left him with a distinctive scar and protruding canine tooth, but it apparently didn't slow down his appetite.

This summer, Chunk was largely absent from Brooks River during the salmon run before returning in September with a substantial belly. Park officials aren't sure where he spent most of his summer. But wherever he was, he wasn't skipping meals.

And he's going to need every pound. His title defense begins Wednesday against Bear 164, Bucky, one of the river's emerging heavyweights.

Bucky has grown considerably in recent years, developing the size and confidence to challenge other dominant males for access to the best fishing spots.

He's also figured out a pretty clever way to keep himself fed.

While other bears compete for the same prime real estate at Brooks Falls, Bucky has learned to position himself near the waterfall's deepest plunge pool, where he can catch salmon jumping through the air, rising from below or falling from above.

And at approximately 9 years old, Bucky is still relatively young. Male brown bears typically reach their physical prime between ages 12 and 20, so he could have several more years of growth ahead of him.

The rising star gets his shot at the defending champion Wednesday, Sept. 23. One of them will be going home early.

Well, metaphorically. They'll both still be in Alaska eating fish.

Bear 151, Walker, used to be a relatively easygoing guy who enjoyed playing with other bears. As he's gotten older, though, he's become a little grumpier and a lot more competitive.

And the younger bears are giving him plenty of reasons to be grumpy.

WILDLIFE PHOTOGRAPHER STAYS ICE-COLD AS MASSIVE BROWN BEAR WALKS RIGHT UP TO HIS CAMERA

Bucky and Bear 903, Gully, have been challenging Walker's position in the Brooks River hierarchy. His size and experience have helped him maintain his standing, but the younger competition is catching up.

Walker faces Gully in Wednesday's opening round, giving us another veteran-versus-youngster matchup right out of the gate.

Check out the rump on this guy, by the way.

Bear 610 might not be one of the biggest competitors in this year's field, but she's got a pretty compelling story.

When she was first identified in 2015, park officials believed she had separated from her mother earlier than expected. She also had a significant healing wound above her hips, suggesting she'd survived an attack.

Now, more than a decade later, she's raising her first known litter of cubs.

Despite being a relatively small, first-time mother, 610 has successfully protected and cared for both cubs throughout the summer while building up her own fat reserves ahead of hibernation.

This is her first Fat Bear Week appearance, and she'll face Bear 89, Backpack, in Wednesday's opening round.

Of course, Fat Bear Week isn't just about which bear has the biggest belly. The competition celebrates the remarkable transformations these animals undergo as they prepare to survive months of winter hibernation without eating or drinking.

The opening round takes place Sept. 22–23, followed by the quarterfinals Sept. 24–25, the Final Fat Four on Sept. 28 and the championship on Sept. 29.

You can view the complete bracket and cast your votes on the official Fat Bear Week website. Voting is open from noon to 9 p.m. ET on tournament days.

item.title: America and China are fighting for the future of AI — chips are the battlefield
item.description: President Donald Trump and Xi Jinping meet in Washington as Huawei races to build a rival AI chip ecosystem that could displace American semiconductor dominance.
item.content:encoded:
When President Donald Trump sits down with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington this week, the agenda will be crowded.

Trade. Tariffs. Rare earth minerals. National security. Supply chains.

But looming over all of it is a technological competition that could shape the balance of economic and military power for decades: artificial intelligence. And increasingly, the battle isn't simply about who builds the best AI model.

TRUMP-XI’S CHINA SUMMIT IS A DEFINING TEST FOR AMERICA IN THE NEW COLD WAR

It is about who controls the chips, computing infrastructure and technology ecosystem underneath it.

America remains the global leader in advanced AI technology and semiconductor design. But China is pushing aggressively to reduce its dependence on American technology, and Huawei has emerged as one of the most important companies in that effort. That should have Washington's full attention.

For years, the United States has used export controls to restrict China's access to advanced semiconductors and semiconductor-manufacturing technology, particularly technologies with potential military applications.

Those restrictions had a clear national-security objective: prevent America's most sophisticated technology from strengthening a strategic competitor's military capabilities. But there has also been an unintended consequence worth confronting. China accelerated its effort to build an AI ecosystem that doesn't need America.

AI 'DOOMERS' RISK KNEECAPPING US VS CHINA, BUT EX-PENTAGON VET SAYS BOTH EXTREMES MISS THE MARK

Huawei expanded its Ascend AI-chip roadmap. Chinese developers adapted software and models to domestic hardware. Chinese companies poured resources into computing systems capable of compensating for some of the performance limitations of individual Chinese chips. And Huawei isn't standing still.

The company recently said demand for its AI computing equipment in China is exceeding supply. It is accelerating future generations of its Ascend processors and developing enormous computing systems capable of connecting vast numbers of chips.

That means the strategic question facing Washington has changed.

AMERICA RUNS ON DATA. IF WE DON’T BUILD THE INFRASTRUCTURE, CHINA WILL

The question isn't simply: How do we keep sensitive American technology away from China? It is also: How do we make sure the rest of the world continues choosing American technology instead of China's? Those are related questions, but they aren't identical.

If American technology becomes inaccessible across too much of the global market, China has an enormous incentive to develop substitutes. Huawei has an enormous incentive to sell them. And governments and companies around the world have an enormous incentive to build around whatever technology they can reliably obtain.

THE AI REVOLUTION COULD BECOME A NATIONAL SECURITY DISASTER IF WE AREN'T CAREFUL

Once developers write software for an ecosystem, companies construct computing infrastructure around it and countries invest billions deploying it, switching becomes much harder. That's why this isn't merely a chip-sales competition. It is an ecosystem competition.

America wants a world running on American chips, American software, American standards and American innovation. China wants to build an alternative. It wants a world in which Huawei and other Chinese companies provide a technology stack that Beijing controls and America cannot easily influence.

President Trump has taken a different approach from the Biden administration. His administration rescinded the Biden-era AI Diffusion Rule while maintaining controls targeting technologies with serious national-security implications.

The administration has also allowed certain advanced chips to be considered for sale to approved Chinese customers under licensing requirements and security conditions. The theory is straightforward: protect the technologies most critical to national security without unnecessarily surrendering commercial markets to Chinese competitors. That distinction matters.

CHINA IS BUILDING AN AI WAR MACHINE. WASHINGTON MUST WAKE UP BEFORE IT’S TOO LATE

Nobody serious is arguing that America should simply hand China unrestricted access to technology that could materially enhance advanced weapons, military AI, surveillance or other sensitive capabilities.

National security comes first. But there is a difference between protecting America's crown-jewel technology and adopting restrictions so sweeping that they accelerate China's determination to replace American technology throughout the commercial market. Because Huawei's goal isn't merely to survive American restrictions.

Huawei wants to compete. It wants Chinese chips powering Chinese AI. It wants Chinese computing infrastructure supporting Chinese models. And ultimately, Chinese technology companies want customers outside China using their systems.

That's why the next phase of this competition will be fought over which chips countries buy, which computing systems they install, which software developers learn and which technology stack becomes the default infrastructure for the AI economy.

America has enormous advantages. We have extraordinary semiconductor designers, the world's leading AI companies, deep capital markets, world-class universities, entrepreneurs and an innovation culture China has spent decades trying to replicate.

But technological leadership isn't permanent. It has to be defended. And sometimes the greatest threat to American leadership isn't that China suddenly invents something better. It's that America creates policies that make its own technology harder for the world to use while Beijing aggressively offers an alternative.

There are already calls for the United States to slow AI development or impose broader restrictions in the name of safety and security. Those arguments deserve serious debate.

AI presents real risks. Advanced semiconductor technology has genuine military applications. Export controls can be an important national-security tool. But every restriction also has consequences.

The question should be whether a restriction actually improves American security without unnecessarily strengthening China's competing technology ecosystem. Because China isn't pausing. Huawei isn't pausing. And global demand for AI computing certainly isn't pausing.

Somebody will provide the chips. Somebody will provide the computing infrastructure. Somebody will provide the software. Somebody will establish the standards.

The United States has a direct strategic interest in American companies remaining central to that ecosystem.

The previous generation of American leaders watched too much manufacturing capacity and too many strategically important supply chains migrate overseas. We should not repeat that mistake with the infrastructure of artificial intelligence.

Semiconductors are no longer merely components inside computers. Compute is strategic power.

The nations and companies controlling advanced computing will possess enormous advantages in scientific discovery, medicine, manufacturing, intelligence, cybersecurity and military technology. That is why the Trump-Xi meeting matters far beyond whatever trade agreement or diplomatic communiqué emerges from Washington.

The two presidents represent countries competing over something much larger: Who builds the technological infrastructure of the 21st century?

The United States should protect its most sensitive technology, its intellectual property and technologies with significant military applications. At the same time, American companies will continue competing for commercial markets around the world.

Design the chips here. Build the semiconductor infrastructure here. Develop the software here. Protect the technology that truly must be protected. And keep American technology innovative and competitive enough that countries around the world continue choosing the American ecosystem instead of Huawei's.

The AI Cold War is already underway. And the chips are the battlefield.

item.title: 1619 Project founder regrets school choice for her daughter, admits putting ideals ahead of her education
item.description: Nikole Hannah-Jones says she regrets her Brooklyn public school choice after her daughter said she never got the education she truly wanted.
item.content:encoded:
Nikole Hannah-Jones, New York Times Magazine reporter and creator of the controversial 1619 Project, acknowledged Sunday that she regretted aspects of the decision to send her daughter to predominantly Black, high-poverty public schools in Brooklyn, New York, after the now-16-year-old told her she did not receive the education she wanted — a decade after Hannah-Jones described the choice as an effort to challenge school segregation.

In a newly released New York Times Magazine essay, Hannah-Jones described revisiting years of emails with her daughter Najya’s teachers and principals and confronting what she called a truth she could no longer suppress.

"Now I felt overcome with regret. Najya deserved better," Hannah-Jones said. "They all did. But she was mine. This girl, my only child, looked to me to protect her, to give her what she needed to thrive. And I had not chosen her."

Hannah-Jones told Fox News Digital on Sunday that the broader focus should remain on families who lack the resources to pursue better educational options for their children.

"I hope people concerned about the choice my husband and I made for our daughter will have equal or more outrage for the thousands of Black children whose parents don’t have the resources to send them to better schools," she said. "As I write in the piece, there is no absolution to be had for any of us."

POWERFUL TEACHERS' UNIONS SHARE STRIKING LINK WITH STATES STRUGGLING TO TEACH KIDS TO READ

Corey DeAngelis, a research fellow at The Heritage Foundation and longtime school choice advocate, responded to Hannah-Jones' essay in a statement to Fox News Digital, arguing parents should prioritize their children's individual educational needs.

"Parents should put their children first. They should not sacrifice them to a failing government school system in the name of ideology," DeAngelis said. "Nikole Hannah-Jones now says she regrets putting her ideals ahead of her daughter’s education. That admission is long overdue."

"I welcome Nikole Hannah-Jones to the school choice revolution," he continued. "Maybe she will start to understand that pulling her daughter from the failing school system would have done more to improve those schools — through competition — than the status quo ever did. You don’t fix public schools by locking kids in them without any accountability. You fix them by giving them a reason to change their ways."

NEW YORK JOINS FEDERAL SCHOOL CHOICE INITIATIVE DESPITE TRADITIONAL DEMOCRAT OPPOSITION

Hannah-Jones said the realization culminated in a conversation with Najya as she was writing the essay. She apologized to her daughter after reviewing problems that had followed her through elementary and middle school.

"I feel like you got cheated," Hannah-Jones said. "And I’m sorry for that."

Najya responded by telling her mother that she wished her own education had received greater consideration alongside Hannah-Jones' broader concerns about educational inequality.

"Sometimes I wish instead of always thinking about other kids, you would have thought about me. I never really got the education I wanted," Najya said.

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION TOUTS ‘HARD RESET’ FOR AMERICAN SCHOOLS, VOWS TO PUT PARENTS ‘BACK IN CHARGE’

Hannah-Jones’ assessment marked a shift from the position she described in a widely discussed 2016 New York Times Magazine essay, when she explained why she and her husband enrolled Najya at P.S. 307, a Brooklyn school that was then overwhelmingly Black and Latino and served a largely low-income population. Hannah-Jones said at the time she believed middle-class families could help improve segregated schools by enrolling their children and investing in them.

"I worried — I worry still — about whether I made the right decision for our little girl. But I knew I made the just one," Hannah-Jones said in 2016.

The new essay detailed academic problems that became more apparent as Najya grew older. At Unison, her middle school, Najya earned strong grades and took honors courses, but later said she and her friends realized that they were not being sufficiently challenged. 

Hannah-Jones described limited homework, inexperienced teachers and gaps in her daughter's math preparation that became especially apparent after Najya entered a more academically demanding high school.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Unison Principal Emily Paige acknowledged in the essay that some attempts to accommodate students who entered the school academically behind had unintended consequences, including the decision to eliminate homework.

"It is important to not, in our pursuit of being antiracist, lower expectations," Paige said. "Because this is what happens, right? It’s racism under the guise of antiracism."

DeAngelis told Fox News Digital that Hannah-Jones’ experience should lead her to support policies allowing education funding to follow children to schools selected by their families.

"Hannah-Jones can afford better options. Most families cannot," DeAngelis said. "She should fight for the funding to follow the student so more parents have the same educational opportunities she can buy for herself. School choice is an equalizer."

The debate comes as school choice remains an active issue in New York.

Fox News Digital reported last week that teachers' unions were opposing Democratic New York Gov. Kathy Hochul's plan to participate in a federal tax-credit scholarship program designed to help families pay for educational options outside their assigned schools.

The New York Times' 1619 Project is a long-form collaboration that seeks to "reframe the country's history" by bringing slavery and racism to the forefront of the national narrative. 

While praised by liberals, the project has faced intense scrutiny and pushback from prominent historians who have publicly disputed its factual accuracy, particularly its claims regarding the motivations behind the American Revolution.

Despite the criticism, the 1619 Project's theories of American history were later developed into an educational curriculum with the help of the Pulitzer Center.

Fox News Digital reached out to New York Public Schools for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: DHS chief fires back at Jayapal over claim majority of immigration arrests pose 'no threat'
item.description: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin rejected Pramila Jayapal's claim that most ICE arrests over the summer involved individuals who pose "no threat" to public safety, citing angel families.
item.content:encoded:
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin pushed back on Rep. Pramila Jayapal’s, D-Wash., claim that the "majority of people" arrested by DHS pose "absolutely no threat to public safety."

Mullin rejected Jayapal’s characterization on "Saturday in America," saying DHS and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) remain committed to targeting high-risk individuals to keep American communities safe and arguing that crimes committed by illegal immigrants have led to tragedy.

"If we're going to have national security in this country, we [need to] know everybody that's entered this country. And so, I'm not going to release you back into the public once we know that you entered this country illegally," Mullin said. "It's time for you to go home."

BORDER CZAR TOM HOMAN FIRES BACK AFTER DEMOCRAT CHRIS MURPHY CLAIMS ICE IS ‘TERRORIZING LITTLE KIDS’

"All the angel families that lost their loved ones at the hands of an illegal is 100% preventable, because that illegal shouldn't be in our country to begin with," the DHS boss added.

Jayapal, the ranking member of the House Subcommittee on Immigration, Integrity, Security, and Enforcement and a vocal ICE critic, argued that immigration enforcement under the Trump administration has targeted immigrants without criminal convictions.

"For the first time this summer, the majority of people that DHS arrested were people who pose absolutely no threat to public safety, and the number of people with criminal convictions who are arrested by ICE actually decreased — decreased, not increased," Jayapal said during a hearing last week.

"That’s because when DHS expends all of its energy to go after parents, longtime friends, neighbors, when [Homeland Security Investigations] agents who are supposed to investigate serious crime and human trafficking are instead being moved to street sweeps and riding along with local police for random traffic stops, we are less safe, not more safe," she added.

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION'S IMMIGRATION PUSH FUELS ICE'S BIGGEST ARREST MONTH IN AGENCY HISTORY

DHS SECRETARY BASHES NEW YORK LEADERSHIP AFTER ANNOUNCING THOUSANDS OF ARRESTS IN SWEEPING OPERATION

ICE arrested nearly 51,000 illegal immigrants nationwide in August, marking the highest monthly total on record, according to DHS. The department also says ICE has deported more than 2,000 known or suspected terrorists since Trump took office.

"When you have a car accident, and you came… into this country legally, and the Democrats want to say, you're not a criminal and you kill somebody. Yes, you were a criminal and now… you ruined somebody else's life, and now you're a murderer at the same time," the DHS chief said.

"It's political for them. They want to say this every day," he added.

DHS regularly publicizes arrests and deportations involving illegal immigrants convicted of crimes including murder, child pornography, sexual assault and drug trafficking.

"When you decide you're going to break our immigration policies, and you're going to cut the line, you're going to step across our southern border, you're going to step across our northern border. You're still a criminal. We’re still gonna arrest you," the DHS chief said.

Fox News Digital reached out to Jayapal’s office for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: Nicki Minaj offers career advice to young Americans, delivers blunt response to Trump critics
item.description: Rapper Nicki Minaj revealed her path from Red Lobster to global stardom and fiercely defended her support of President Donald Trump in an exclusive interview.
item.content:encoded:
Rapper Nicki Minaj shared her career advice to young Americans entering the workforce and fiercely defended her support of President Donald Trump during an exclusive interview with "The Ingraham Angle" on Friday.

The music mogul opened up about her journey to the top, explaining how she hustled her way from serving biscuits at Red Lobster to dominating music charts around the world and collaborating with some of the biggest names in Hollywood.

"I did customer service for telephone companies. I was a telemarketer. I sold fire extinguishers. I did everything," Minaj shared with Fox News.

NICKI MINAJ, ANNA NICOLE SMITH AND MORE STARS WHO GOT THEIR START WAITING TABLES AT RED LOBSTER

MARY J BLIGE CREDITS FAITH, PASTORS WITH CONFRONTING HER PRIDE AS SHE TOOK CONTROL OF HER CAREER

"What I would tell young people is: This is not the best part of your life, but it is probably one of the most important parts of your life," she said.

Minaj said the lessons she learned, as well as the values she developed while doing "nitty-gritty" work, before money and international success, remain central to how she conducts business today.

"The things that I learned during that time in my life, it still helps me today," the rapper explained. "All the people skills, and the communication skills, and all the problem-solving that I learned then, it still applies now when I'm around superstars or rich people."

"All of those skills, they carry over into the rest of your life. So don't look at that part of your life as something that you can't wait to fly by because… you might not be making the biggest money, but you're doing the real nitty-gritty work that is going to help you for the rest of your life," Minaj added.

THE RICH HAVE ONE FINANCIAL HABIT MOST AMERICANS IGNORE AT THEIR PERIL

The "Super Bass" and "Starships" singer, who has an estimated net worth of $150 million according to Celebrity Net Worth, also advised young Americans to save money, saying that "no matter how little" she made, she would always set aside funds for a rainy day.

Minaj also discussed her support for President Donald Trump after emerging as one of his fiercest allies in Hollywood.

The rapper recently partnered with the Trump administration on the Small Business Administration’s Million Dollar Pitch Competition, serving as one of the celebrity judges.

LIL WAYNE PRAISES TRUMP'S WHITE HOUSE BALLROOM PROJECT, CALLS OUT CRITICS WHO 'DON'T KNOW NOTHING'

The competition brought five small business owners before a panel of judges, including Minaj and Airbnb’s co-founder, to give their best pitch for a share of a $1 million cash prize pool.

"Small business represents the heart of the country…," said Minaj. "You don't have to be a huge household name to be recognized by the president and to be recognized by us."

Minaj, whom Trump has called a "fantastic person," addressed the grief she receives for supporting the president, telling Fox News that she has "absolutely nothing" to say to critics and adding that she is "honored" to work with the administration.

"[Trump] is fun," the rapper said. "He's not just smart and he's not just the president, but he's also someone that I can relate to."

DOLLY PARTON REFUSED TO PICK POLITICAL SIDES FOR DECADES: ‘I’M NOT IN POLITICS, I’M AN ENTERTAINER’

"He's very grounded. It's easy to connect with him, it's easy feel like he heard you, he understands you," she continued. "And I just love him, and I'm not going to ever make excuses for that."

Minaj was also asked when her fans, whom she fondly refers to as "Barbz," can expect her next tour following a hiatus after her Pink Friday 2 World Tour in 2024. 

She urged fans to give her some time as she embraces what she described as her "businesswoman era."

"Who set you up to asking this question? Is one of the Barbz back there?" she asked host Laura Ingraham. "I'm gonna go out as soon as I present the Barbz with this next body of work, whenever that will be."

"Barbz, I love you very much if you're watching, and I don't want any more questions about concerts. I'm in my businesswoman era," she added.

item.title: Scammers are buying Google ads to steal bank logins
item.description: Federal prosecutors say criminals bought sponsored search ads mimicking real banks, capturing over 5,000 login credentials and draining accounts.
item.content:encoded:
You need to check your bank account, so you open Google, type in your bank's name and click the first result that looks right. Most of us have done some version of that without thinking twice.

Now federal investigators say criminals turned that everyday habit into a way to steal bank logins and drain accounts. The Justice Department announced on Sept. 8 that a Russian web developer accused of helping run a large bank account takeover operation had been extradited to the United States. Prosecutors say the group bought sponsored search engine links that sent banking customers to fake login pages. Victims then entered their credentials, believing they had reached their bank.

That should get the attention of anyone who banks online. Here's how the scam works, why those sponsored results can look so convincing and what you can do to avoid handing your bank login to a criminal.

ASKED SIRI TO CALL YOUR BANK? A SCAM COULD COST THOUSANDS

According to federal prosecutors, the alleged operation used spoofed domains that mimicked websites belonging to federally insured financial institutions. The conspirators then bought sponsored search engine links. Those links could appear when someone searched for their bank.

A click sent the customer to a fraudulent login page. Once victims entered their credentials, the attackers could capture that information. Prosecutors say the group then used the stolen credentials to access real bank accounts, check balances and initiate unauthorized wire transfers.

The indictment also alleges that Sergei Anatolyevich Filimonov developed and maintained infrastructure supporting the operation. That included databases storing more than 5,000 stolen login credentials and software designed to capture sensitive authentication data.

The newest Sept. 8 Justice Department announcement says the conspirators purchased sponsored search-engine links. It does not name a particular search engine. However, the DOJ previously described the same bank account takeover operation when it seized the group's backend domain in December 2025. In that announcement, investigators specifically said the criminal group delivered fraudulent advertisements through search engines including Google and Bing. The ads imitated sponsored search ads used by legitimate banks.

Victims who clicked those ads were redirected to fake banking websites controlled by the criminals, according to the DOJ. That earlier investigation had identified at least 19 victims across the United States by December 2025. The DOJ reported approximately $28 million in attempted losses and about $14.6 million in actual losses tied to those victims.

Microsoft told CyberGuy that it has policies and detection mechanisms designed to help prevent misleading advertising. The company said that when it becomes aware of ads that violate its policies, it takes action to remove them and uses what it learns to strengthen its detection capabilities. Microsoft also encourages users to report suspicious ads through its "Report a Concern" form. We also reached out to Google for comment but did not hear back before our deadline.

FAKE PATIENT PORTAL SCAM CAN STEAL YOUR LOGIN AND INFECT YOUR PC

The trap works because a paid search result can appear in a place many of us naturally look first. You search for your bank. A result appears near the top. The wording looks familiar, so you click before studying the address. Most search ads are legitimate.

Still, the FBI warns that criminals can buy ads that imitate real businesses and direct users to convincing phishing sites. The FBI refers to this tactic as SEO poisoning in its account takeover guidance. That changes how I would approach something as sensitive as online banking. In fact, the FBI specifically recommends using bookmarks or favorites to reach login pages rather than clicking search results or advertisements.

This problem stretches far beyond one alleged criminal operation. Since January 2025, the FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center has received more than 5,100 complaints reporting account takeover fraud. Reported losses have exceeded $262 million.

Criminals use several ways to get inside accounts. Fraudulent banking websites remain one of them. The FBI says victims can encounter a phishing site after clicking a fake search advertisement. Attackers may also try to obtain a one-time passcode if an account uses multifactor authentication.

Once criminals gain access, they may move money to accounts they control. That can make recovery difficult, especially when funds move quickly.

The latest development centers on Sergei Anatolyevich Filimonov, 36, a Russian national and web developer. A federal grand jury indicted Filimonov on Nov. 4, 2025. Authorities later extradited him from the Republic of Georgia.

You do not need to stop banking online. However, changing how you reach your bank's login page can lower your risk.

SHOULD YOU USE A SEPARATE COMPUTER FOR ONLINE BANKING?

If you already have your bank's verified app installed, open it directly rather than searching for your bank in a browser. That removes the search-result step where this particular scam tries to catch you.

Visit your bank's verified website and save it as a bookmark or favorite. The FBI specifically recommends bookmarks or favorites for financial login pages instead of relying on search results or advertisements.

Take a second to inspect the domain before you enter banking credentials. A fake site may use a misspelled address or another small change designed to look legitimate. The FBI warns that fraudulent search ads can lead to URLs that closely resemble the real address. Microsoft also advises users to carefully review website URLs before entering credentials or other personal information online.

A "Sponsored" label means someone paid to place the advertisement. So when money or sensitive information is involved, verify the destination yourself before you sign in.

Enable two-factor or multifactor authentication if your financial institution offers it. However, do not let that give you a false sense of security. The FBI warns that MFA may not protect you after you land on a fraudulent login page. Criminals can also use social engineering to try to obtain your one-time code. Never give a one-time passcode to someone who contacts you unexpectedly.

YOUR BANK MAY STOP TEXTING YOU SIX-DIGIT CODES

A trusted password manager can help because it associates your saved login with a particular website. If your password manager normally fills your banking credentials but suddenly does not, stop before typing them manually. Check the address first. We've previously explained how password managers can provide another clue when you land on a spoofed login page.

Strong antivirus software can add another layer of protection if you click a malicious search result. It may warn you about known phishing sites, block dangerous downloads and stop other threats before they reach your device. However, no security software can protect you if you willingly enter your banking credentials on a convincing fake site, so always check the web address first. Set up alerts for activity such as withdrawals and new logins if your bank offers them. Then review unexpected activity immediately. The FBI recommends regularly monitoring financial accounts for unauthorized transactions.

Identity theft protection can help monitor for signs that your personal information is being misused. Some services can alert you to suspicious activity involving your credit, financial accounts or personal information and provide recovery assistance if fraud occurs. This will not stop a fake bank ad, but it can give you another way to spot trouble after your information has been exposed. If you think you entered your credentials on a fake banking page, contact your financial institution immediately using a number you trust. Then reset the exposed credentials. If you reused the same password on another account, change it there as well. The FBI also recommends reporting fraudulent wire transfers to the Internet Crime Complaint Center at IC3.gov. Acting quickly may improve the chances of stopping or reversing a transfer.

What gets me about this scam is how normal the first step feels. You want to check your balance, so you search for your bank and choose a result that appears legitimate. There may be no strange email waiting in your inbox. You did not respond to an unexpected text. You started the search yourself. That can make the trap much harder to recognize. For banking, I would skip search results altogether. Use your bank's official app or a bookmark you have already verified. Then take a moment to look at the address before entering anything sensitive. A few extra seconds can be a lot easier than trying to recover money after it has left your account.

item.title: See inside the abandoned 95-year-old LA church that just became a luxury hotel
item.description: Hotel Lucile transformed a 1931 Silver Lake church in Los Angeles into a 25-room boutique hotel, preserving stained glass and wood flooring.
item.content:encoded:
A building that has stood in Los Angeles for nearly a century is welcoming visitors in an entirely new way after an extensive restoration.

The former Bethany Presbyterian Church, built in 1931 in the city's Silver Lake neighborhood, has been converted into Hotel Lucile, a 25-room boutique hotel with a courtyard cocktail pool that opened Sept. 14, according to a hotel news release shared with Fox News Digital.

The property has taken on several roles over the decades. After operating as a church, it was later used as a theater and an antique market before being converted into a hotel, according to the release.

RENTALS NOW ALLOWED IN HISTORIC WATER TOWER ON KING CHARLES' SANDRINGHAM ESTATE WHERE ROYALS SPEND CHRISTMAS

The latest transformation was about seven and a half years in the making, Anthony Gutierrez, opening general manager of Hotel Lucile, told Fox News Digital.

The restoration focused on finding a new use for the building while maintaining elements that date to its time as a house of worship, Gutierrez said.

Many of the church's original features remain throughout the property, including stained-glass windows, wooden beams, high ceilings and steel-framed windows.

One of the biggest transformations took place inside the former chapel, which now serves as the hotel's restaurant and dining room.

"Literally just about every aspect of the chapel itself was preserved," Gutierrez said, pointing to the original wood flooring, beams and stained-glass windows.

Preserving those features while preparing the building for its new use required extensive work, Gutierrez said. Crews removed the chapel's original wood flooring to install modern electrical and plumbing systems and add soundproofing for the guest rooms before putting the flooring back into place.

"For the dining room itself, it is as original as it can be," he said, estimating that about 90% of the space remains original.

Working with a building approaching 100 years old also presented challenges throughout the years-long redevelopment.
